PullRequest.Title: Support activity bar on top of primary side bar
PullRequest.Body: - Activity bar position setting that supports side, top of primary side bar and hidden. - Deprecated activity bar visibility setting in favour of this new setting - Top position is supported only in custom title bar mode - Global actions (account, gear) are shown in title bar to the right and badges are supported

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The subscription, singleton service lifetime, eager per-container action creation, MutableDisposable teardown, and absence of a PaneCompositeBar-wide action disposal are all directly visible. The exact number of user toggles varies, but retention and linear growth occur for every completed cycle.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained ViewContainerActivityAction objects and ActivityService emitter listeners, plus repeated callback CPU on each badge update.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For V registered sidebar view containers and T completed top-to-non-top transitions, the service retains O(V*T) dead actions/listeners; each subsequent activity event dispatches across the same growing listener set.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained memory and steadily increasing synchronous badge-update CPU over the window lifetime.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: ActivityService delegated badge updates directly to the currently selected pane composite bar, and ViewContainerActivityAction did not subscribe to a singleton service, so discarding a bar did not leave each action rooted by a long-lived emitter.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every ViewContainerActivityAction now registers itself on the singleton ActivityService emitter. The new top-position UI creates a fresh PaneCompositeBar for every side/hidden-to-top transition and clears that bar when leaving top, but PaneCompositeBar keeps these actions in a plain Map and has no whole-map disposal path.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `this._register(this.activityService.onDidChangeActivity(...))` roots each per-container action in the long-lived ActivityService; the same PR adds transient top-bar construction and teardown via SidebarPart/updateTitleArea.
Findings.Title: Dispose activity listeners when replacing the top bar
Findings.Impact: After toggling the activity bar from top back to side/hidden, one action and listener per registered sidebar view container remains retained. Repeating the toggle grows heap usage by O(view containers × toggles), and every later SCM/Problems/debug badge change synchronously walks the accumulated dead listeners, progressively increasing UI-thread work.
Findings.Evidence: SidebarPart's configuration listener calls updateTitleArea; the top branch creates an ActivityBarCompositeBar, whose PaneCompositeBar constructor calls onDidRegisterViewContainers and getCompositeActions for every sidebar container. Leaving top calls paneCompositeBar.clear(), but only individual hideComposite/removeComposite paths dispose actions. Therefore this added subscription survives disposal of the transient bar and ActivityService retains each action callback.
Findings.Recommendation: Own all entries of compositeActions with a disposable collection and dispose/clear every activity, pinned, and badge action when PaneCompositeBar is disposed (or keep one stable bar instead of recreating it), so clearing the top bar unregisters every ActivityService listener.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Both construction paths and the uncached per-provider getSessions call are explicit, and the provider implementation demonstrably crosses the extension-host boundary. Initialization is scheduled after restore/idle, so the exact visible latency varies, but the duplicate call cardinality is deterministic in top mode.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Authentication-provider getSessions IPC calls and duplicate account-controller objects/listeners.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold top-mode initialization grows from P to 2P concurrent getSessions calls for P registered providers; each later reconstruction of the title-bar account item adds another P-call initialization pass.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC/provider work and avoidable post-startup CPU/network activity.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: There was one AccountsActivityActionViewItem owned by the activity bar, so startup account discovery issued one getSessions request per registered authentication provider.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When the activity bar location is top, the new title-bar toolbar instantiates SimpleAccountActivityActionViewItem in addition to the AccountsActivityActionViewItem already constructed by the ActivitybarPart's GlobalCompositeBar. Each instance independently registers authentication listeners and runs its own post-restore account initialization.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added actionViewItemProvider branch creates `SimpleAccountActivityActionViewItem`; that subclass invokes the same eager initializer as the pre-existing activity-bar account view item instead of sharing its loaded account state.
Findings.Title: Avoid initializing a second accounts controller for the top bar
Findings.Impact: Starting or switching into top mode after restoration issues two extension-host session queries per authentication provider and duplicates account aggregation/listeners. Providers may perform storage or network-backed session work, adding avoidable background IPC and extension-host load; re-entering top repeats the extra fan-out.
Findings.Evidence: SimpleAccountActivityActionViewItem subclasses AccountsActivityActionViewItem, whose constructor calls initialize(); doInitialize maps every provider to addAccountsFromProvider(), which calls authenticationService.getSessions(providerId). MainThreadAuthenticationProvider.getSessions crosses to the extension host through `$getSessions`. SidebarPart always constructs ActivitybarPart and its GlobalCompositeBar even when the grid activity bar is hidden for the top setting, so top mode has two concurrent initializers rather than replacing the first.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep account discovery in one shared controller/model and have both renderers subscribe to it, or suppress construction/initialization of the hidden side-bar global account item while the title-bar instance is active.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start the workbench with the activity bar at the side and process view/global badge changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench construction eagerly creates the side ActivitybarPart, PaneCompositeBar actions, and global action view items. Badge publication synchronously mutates ActivityService maps, fires its emitter, and updates the matching action/DOM before the caller returns; account discovery is deferred until Restored and idle, so it is off startup's initial critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch authentication sessions from each extension-contributed provider through MainThreadAuthenticationProvider.$getSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per registered provider from the single side-bar AccountsActivityActionViewItem; providers run concurrently through Promise.allSettled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing activity-bar accounts item already issued one request per provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred until the workbench is restored and idle, so it adds background post-startup load rather than blocking initial rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered view containers controls synchronous emitter listeners; number of authentication providers controls deferred account-session requests; badge event frequency comes from SCM, Problems, debug, testing, and extension views.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Badge dispatch is synchronous and serial across listeners. Authentication providers are queried concurrently once per provider by Promise.allSettled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Activity arrays are held in ActivityService maps and matching actions read them directly. The accounts item has a private groupedAccounts cache, with no sharing across item instances.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: construction, event delivery, and provider RPC paths are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical view-container count and badge churn vary by installed extensions, but side mode alone remains lifetime-bounded and account query cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for normal side mode: the new shared emitter adds bounded in-memory fan-out, but without repeated top-bar teardown it does not establish an independently material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or switch the workbench into top activity-bar mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changing the setting synchronously rebuilds the sidebar title area and lays it out. The title-bar accounts item then schedules account discovery after Restored/idle; those provider calls are off the immediate layout critical path but run as background extension-host work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Each AccountsActivityActionViewItem calls authenticationService.getSessions for every registered provider, which invokes extension-host $getSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two independent account items issue 2P calls for P providers in top mode: the always-constructed side ActivitybarPart item plus the title-bar item. Every later reconstruction of the title-bar item adds another P-call pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the side activity-bar accounts item existed, producing P calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred to idle after restoration, but consumes extension-host/provider capacity and may trigger provider storage or network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the activity-bar location configuration value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration write per position command, equivalent in cardinality to the prior visibility-setting update for hide/show.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Visibility changes also updated one workbench configuration key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command awaits no explicit result, while configuration listeners synchronously rebuild layout state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and store pinned/placeholder view-container state while constructing the top PaneCompositeBar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: saveCachedViewContainers is reached once per registered sidebar container during construction, although equality checks can suppress unchanged backing-store writes; serialization still scans the current composite collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No additional PaneCompositeBar was dynamically constructed when toggling activity-bar visibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously during the setting-triggered title-area rebuild.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P authentication providers and V registered/cached sidebar view containers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two account controllers independently issue their P-provider batches; each batch uses Promise.allSettled, so up to 2P provider calls can overlap. Top-bar construction and state serialization are synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The hidden side account controller and title-bar account controller maintain separate groupedAccounts maps, so warm state in one does not prevent the other's provider queries. PaneCompositeBar reads cached container metadata but rebuilds actions and serializes state for the new instance.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both account instances, their eager initialization, and the uncached provider RPC are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations differ in cost and may cache internally; the duplicate IPC count is deterministic. View-container counts are usually modest, so the construction-time serialization alone was not reported.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the deterministic duplicate per-provider session discovery added by the title-bar account item.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle activity bar top, then side or hidden, repeatedly; later receive badge updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each transition to top synchronously constructs one action per sidebar view container. Leaving top disposes the PaneCompositeBar through MutableDisposable, but its plain compositeActions map is not disposed wholesale. Later badge publications synchronously dispatch through ActivityService before callers return.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: V registered sidebar view containers, T top-to-non-top cycles, and E later activity events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Construction, teardown, and event delivery are synchronous on the UI thread. Each event serially invokes the emitter's listener set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A fresh top-bar action map is created on every entry to top. The ActivityService emitter retains callbacks from disposed bars, preventing those action objects from becoming collectible; there is no eviction/coalescing for these stale listeners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: action creation for all containers, singleton-emitter registration, MutableDisposable teardown, and missing map disposal are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users toggle layout infrequently, but every completed cycle deterministically retains V listeners and the cost persists for the window lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported unbounded listener/action retention and the resulting O(V*T) memory plus future badge-dispatch work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize and render the activity bar in side or top orientation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Grid layout invokes ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout, which reads menu/global element dimensions before laying out the composite bar; top mode uses the sidebar title area's existing part layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize frequency and number of visible composite actions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous UI-thread DOM/layout work; no asynchronous queue or coalescing is introduced here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Composite sizes and action models remain in memory; no external cache boundary is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability, insufficient evidence of a material regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM geometry reads can force style resolution, but the changed code does not establish a new repeated read-after-write loop on normal resize, and top mode does not construct global controls inside this layout method.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the geometry reads are bounded per layout and largely preserve the previous vertical activity-bar behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 30 changed files and all diff pages. Reported two introduced regressions: leaked ActivityService listeners/actions across top-bar teardown cycles, and duplicate per-provider authentication session IPC in top mode. Checked startup, setting transitions, badge updates, rendering/layout, storage/serialization, cache behavior, and effective concurrency; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
